LunaScope – Smart Lunar Landing Site Evaluation System

LunaScope is an interactive web-based platform designed to explore and compare potential lunar landing regions, with a focus on NASA's Artemis III candidate regions near the lunar south pole. It features a 3D interactive Moon that allows users to rotate, zoom, and select candidate regions to view their names, approximate locations, and descriptions.

The platform also provides a site analysis interface and a comparison tool to help users examine the geographical characteristics of different candidate regions. By presenting lunar locations through an accessible visual interface, LunaScope makes complex lunar exploration information easier to understand and explore.

LunaScope addresses the challenge of identifying and evaluating potential lunar landing locations by bringing candidate-region information together in one interactive platform. It aims to support awareness, exploration, and preliminary mission-planning discussions while highlighting the importance of safe and scientifically valuable landing locations for future human exploration of the Moon.
details:
LunaScope – Smart Lunar Landing Site Evaluation System

1.Project Overview

LunaScope is an interactive, web-based lunar exploration platform developed to visualize and explore potential landing regions near the Moon's south pole. It focuses on the nine candidate regions identified by NASA for the Artemis III mission.

The main objective of LunaScope is to make lunar landing-region information easier to access, understand and compare through an interactive 3D environment.

2.How Does LunaScope Work?

LunaScope provides users with an interactive representation of the Moon and a set of tools for exploring candidate landing regions.

Interactive 3D Moon Explorer:
Users can rotate and zoom the 3D Moon to explore its surface. Candidate landing regions are marked directly on the lunar globe. When a user selects a marker, the platform displays the region's name, description and approximate geographical coordinates.

NASA Candidate Region Explorer:
The platform includes all nine NASA Artemis III candidate regions: Peak near Cabeus B, Haworth, Malapert Massif, Mons Mouton Plateau, Mons Mouton, Nobile Rim 1, Nobile Rim 2, de Gerlache Rim 2 and Slater Plain.

Site Analysis:
Users can select a candidate region, view its approximate latitude and longitude, and record a planned landing date. The interface also presents fields for terrain, illumination and landing suitability, which are currently identified as unavailable because the corresponding scientific datasets have not yet been integrated.

Region Comparison:
Users can select multiple candidate regions and compare their geographical latitudes through an interactive chart and comparison table. This provides a simple way to examine the geographical distribution of the selected locations.

3.Benefits and Intended Impact

LunaScope aims to make lunar exploration information more accessible through visualization and organized geographical data.

Its potential benefits include simplifying the exploration of lunar south-pole candidate regions, helping users understand the geographical distribution of potential landing locations, providing an interactive way to explore NASA's Artemis III candidate regions, bringing location information, site analysis and comparison features together in one platform, and supporting educational activities and introductory discussions about lunar exploration and future human missions.

The intended impact is to encourage greater awareness of lunar exploration and provide an accessible starting point for understanding the considerations involved in selecting potential lunar landing locations.

4.Technologies and Tools Used

LunaScope was developed as a browser-based application using HTML5 for the structure and organization of the web application, CSS3 for visual design and styling, and JavaScript for interactive functionality, region selection, data handling and user interactions.

Three.js was used to render the interactive 3D Moon, while Chart.js was used to display geographical comparisons through charts. NASA lunar imagery provides visual surface information for the 3D Moon. GitHub was used for source-code storage, and GitHub Pages was used to host and deploy the application as a publicly accessible website.

The application does not require a dedicated backend server and can be accessed through a modern web browser.

5.Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of LunaScope lies in combining a 3D lunar visualization with geographical exploration and comparison tools in a single web platform.

Instead of presenting candidate landing regions only as names or static lists, LunaScope places them on an interactive lunar globe. Users can rotate the Moon, select individual markers, explore location information and compare multiple regions.

This visual approach makes lunar exploration more engaging and understandable, particularly for students, educators and people interested in space science.

6.Factors Considered During Development

The development of LunaScope was guided by several important considerations, including geographical relevance by focusing on NASA's identified Artemis III candidate regions near the lunar south pole, accessibility through a simple interface, visualization through a rotatable and zoomable 3D globe, and usability through clearly organized location details, analysis and comparison tools.

Scientific accuracy was also considered by distinguishing approximate reference coordinates from authoritative landing-site measurements and avoiding unsupported claims about landing suitability. Expandability was another consideration, with the platform designed so that additional verified lunar datasets and newly identified regions can be incorporated in future development.

7.Future Scope

LunaScope has the potential to evolve into a more comprehensive lunar landing-site exploration platform through the integration of authoritative scientific datasets.

Future improvements may include high-resolution lunar elevation and slope data, illumination and shadow analysis, communication visibility assessment, and more detailed scientific evaluation of candidate regions.

The platform could also be extended to incorporate new candidate regions as reliable information becomes available.

Conclusion

LunaScope brings lunar geography and interactive technology together to create an accessible platform for exploring potential landing regions. By combining a 3D Moon, NASA candidate-region information, site analysis and comparison features, it provides a foundation for making lunar exploration more visual, understandable and engaging.
